business_problem: BBVA needed to move from early interest in generative AI to an organization-wide operating model that could build on its existing analytics and machine-learning work and prepare the bank for future AI use cases.
solution_summary: BBVA describes its work with IBM as a multiyear generative-AI adoption effort layered on top of the bank's existing analytics and machine-learning programs. Rather than treating gen AI as a plug-and-play feature, the bank says it formed a dedicated team with IBM and approached the work as 'collaborative craftsmanship' involving early awareness, shared experimentation, fine-tuning, and close partnership between business teams and people who understand models deeply. The source does not name a specific IBM product or single deployment architecture, but it does make clear that BBVA is using IBM expertise to operationalize generative AI inside a large banking environment and prepare the organization for future AI use cases. In practice, the solution is an operating model: IBM and BBVA align data, model knowledge, and business context so the bank can move from general enthusiasm about gen AI to a governed transformation program.
business_outcome: BBVA says its work with IBM created early awareness, stronger preparedness, and a practical collaboration model for fine-tuning and scaling generative AI across the bank.
architecture_clues: The page emphasizes a dedicated joint team rather than a single named product deployment.
The operating model combines business teams with people who know models well.
The use case centers on preparation, fine-tuning, and organizational readiness for generative AI.
evidence_quotes: "Through our journey with generative AI, we've seen a remarkable transformation at BBVA."
"It's not just plug & play; it's about collaborative craftsmanship, fine-tuning models"
"The partnership with IBM ... has been instrumental in helping us navigate this transformative path successfully."
